about: The household's keys as one device hands them to another: docs/API.md (Keys). A member wraps a keyring for another device's public key with HPKE (RFC 9180) in auth mode: DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM; info "petcam.keyring.v1"; associated data "petcam.keyring.v1|<household id>|<recipient>|<epoch>", where <epoch> is the keyring's newest and <recipient> the device's id, or "watch" for an Apple Watch's (its iPhone hands it over, never the server). It travels as "<encapsulated key>.<ciphertext and tag>", both base64url.

Inside is JSON as Swift's JSONEncoder writes HouseholdSecret by default, unlike everything else on the wire: camelCase, "householdID", and bytes as standard base64 with padding. {"householdID", "name", "epochs": [{"epoch", "secret", "proof", "takenAt"}], "offICloud"}. Readers take it as values: key order and unknown fields don't matter.

CryptoKit draws its own ephemeral key, so what it seals differs every time: `sealed_by_cryptokit` was sealed once by SharedTests/KeyringVectorTests.swift and recorded (server/scripts/vectors/recorded/cryptokit.json), and `sealed_by_script` by server/scripts/petcam-crypto.mjs with the ephemeral key given. Every implementation opens both, and refuses both as `must_refuse` says.
Bytes are base64url without padding unless a field says hex or base64; strings are UTF-8; "|" joins the parts of a message, with nothing around it.

Made by server/scripts/vectors.mjs from fixed keys that were made up for these files; nothing here was ever a real home's. No vector is ever removed: a format the apps stop opening stays, as one that must fail. Read by SharedTests/KeyringVectorTests.swift and server/test/vectors.test.ts.
name: Home

member.what: a device in the home: it wraps

newcomer.what: the device the keyrings are for

watch.what: an Apple Watch's own key, which only its iPhone knows

stranger.what: a key nothing here was wrapped by or for

approval.what: An approval's keyring: every epoch, so a new device opens older recordings too. Each epoch after the first carries its chain proof.

key_change.what: A key change's keyring: the new epoch alone (the members kept hold the rest), so it has no proof, and stays the same size however many epochs came before.

key_change_off_icloud.what: The same from a device deleting its account: "offICloud": true tells whoever takes the keys to keep them out of iCloud Keychain. Left out when false.

key_change_to_1.what: The key change before that one, to epoch 1.

before_times.what: As builds before 2026-11-10 wrote it: no takenAt.

single_secret.what: As copies from before epochs were saved: one `secret` and no `epochs`. It is epoch 0.

another_order.what: The same kind of thing with its keys in another order, epochs newest first, fields no build knows, "offICloud": false said outright and a name outside ASCII: it reads the same way.

plaintexts_refused.name: secret_base64url
plaintexts_refused.why: the secret as base64url without padding: inside a keyring, bytes are standard base64 with padding

plaintexts_refused.name: epoch_past_the_largest
plaintexts_refused.why: an epoch past 2^31 − 1, the largest a saved copy holds

plaintexts_refused.name: epoch_past_u32
plaintexts_refused.why: an epoch no sealed header could name

plaintexts_refused.name: snake_case
plaintexts_refused.why: household_id: this one object is camelCase (householdID), unlike everything else on the wire

plaintexts_refused.name: no_epochs
plaintexts_refused.why: no epochs, and no single secret either

must_refuse.how: Each wrapped keyring above opens only as it was wrapped: with the recipient's private key, as sent by the member's public key, for its household_id, recipient and epoch. Change any one, and it must not open.

changes.why: as if another key had sent it: auth mode binds the sender's
another device's id (for the Watch's: a device id in place of "watch")
a device's keyring opened as a Watch's, and the Watch's as the newcomer's

inside_mismatch.how: Sealed by the script so that they open, with what's inside at odds with what they were wrapped as: a device checks that the keyring inside is for the household and the epoch it asked for.

cases.name: inside_another_household
cases.why: wrapped as this home's, and inside is another household's id

cases.name: inside_older_epoch
cases.why: wrapped as epoch 2, and the newest epoch inside is 1

cases.name: inside_newer_epoch
cases.why: wrapped as epoch 1, and the newest epoch inside is 2

cases.name: inside_not_a_keyring
cases.why: it opens, and nothing inside is a keyring

catch_up.how: After a key change a device takes the keyrings the server lists for it (GET /v1/household/keyring), oldest first: each only if it is the next epoch, its sender's `from_attestation` checks out under the epoch the device holds now (for `from_device_id` and `from_public_key`), it opens as sent by `from_public_key` for this device, and it agrees with every epoch the device already holds. The first that doesn't ends it. `holder` says which epochs the newcomer starts with; `epoch` is where it ends up.

cases.name: a_key_change
cases.why: the sender is vouched for under epoch 1, the keyring opens as theirs, for this device, and adds epoch 2

cases.name: kept_off_icloud
cases.why: the same, and the keyring says to keep the keys off iCloud Keychain

cases.name: two_in_turn
cases.why: oldest first: epoch 1, then 2 with a sender vouched for under the epoch it just took

cases.name: sender_not_vouched_for
cases.why: the attestation is for another key than the sender's

cases.name: vouched_for_under_the_new_epoch
cases.why: the sender is vouched for under the epoch being handed over, which this device can't check yet: it has to be the one before

cases.name: not_from_the_sender_it_names
cases.why: listed as from a key the home vouches for, but another key wrapped it: it doesn't open as theirs

cases.name: disagrees_about_an_epoch_held
cases.why: it opens, and holds another secret for epoch 1 than this device does: someone is lying

cases.name: skips_an_epoch
cases.why: epoch 2 for a device at epoch 0: only the next epoch is taken

cases.name: the_first_that_fails_ends_it
cases.why: epoch 1 doesn't check out, so epoch 2 is never reached

how: The CFRG's published HPKE test vectors (RFC 9180) for the suite Pet Cam Pro uses: DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256) (kem_id 16), HKDF-SHA256 (kdf_id 1), AES-256-GCM (aead_id 2), in base mode (0) and auth mode (2). The RFC's own appendix prints other suites; this one is in the file the CFRG publishes beside it.

Copied as published, every value hex. Of each mode's 257 encryptions, the six sequence numbers the RFC prints for its suites are kept (0, 1, 2, 4, 255, 256); the exports are left out (the apps export nothing). Pet Cam Pro seals one message per encapsulation: sequence 0.
server/scripts/vectors.mjs copies this into docs/vectors/keyring-v1.json; server/scripts/petcam-crypto.mjs reproduces every value in it.
